references.text: Solomon prays for the foreigner who comes to the temple and loves the name of Israel's God—a parallel to the Gentile officer who loved the Jewish people and built their synagogue.
Cyrus built the temple in Jerusalem and supported the Jewish people, like the Roman officer who built the synagogue for the Jews.
Cornelius was a God-fearing Gentile who gave many gifts to the Jewish people, like the officer in Luke 7 who loved the Jewish people and built the synagogue.
Cornelius was described as one well regarded by all the Jewish people, parallel to the officer whom the elders of the Jews vouched for.
Isaiah prophesies about foreigners joining themselves to the Lord and loving his name—a prophetic background for Gentiles like the Roman officer who loved Israel's people and built their synagogue.

Paul speaks of how Gentiles have shared in the spiritual blessings of the Jews and therefore owe it to serve them with material gifts—a parallel to the officer's gratitude expressed through building the synagogue.
Jesus commends the officer's faith as greater than any he has found in Israel, underscoring that his love for the people was genuine and accompanied by great faith.
